Another part of the product could still stop it at a monthly allowance.\\n\\nThe person using that account shouldn't have to understand why two parts of our system disagreed.\\n\\nThey should be able to rely on what we told them.\\n\\nAlex handled the repair. My responsibility as a founder is to pay attention to the whole promise, including what happens after someone acts on it.\\n\\nI think about the same thing in CPG. A case quantity on a sell sheet. A sample delivery date. The terms in an order email.\\n\\nThose details set an expectation. Then somebody else has to make a decision based on it.\\n\\nA useful check is to read your offer and follow the next few steps as the customer. Where do your words and their experience stop lining up?\\n\\nThat's a question I want us to keep asking at CPG Playbook.\\n\\nTrust gets built in those ordinary details. We have to stay with them.\\r\\n05\\r\\nU-LUV is the first use case I want CPG Playbook to answer to.\\n\\nI have plenty of real work to bring it. Buyers, samples, partners, follow-ups. Questions where the next decision depends on information I don't have in front of me.\\n\\nThat gives Alex and me a practical starting point.\\n\\nTake one task. Work through it. Ask what we'd need to save so we can pick it up again.\\n\\nIf I can't explain where an idea fits in our own food business, I need to keep working on the problem before asking another founder to make room for the solution.\\n\\nIt also keeps me honest about the limits of our experience.\\n\\nA cookie company can't tell us everything about running a beverage brand or a supplement business. What helps me might miss something important in your day.\\n\\nSo U-LUV gives us the starting questions. Other founders need to help us ask better ones.\\n\\nThat's how I want to build this: close enough to the work to notice when we've made an assumption.\\n\\nWhat part of your business would you want us to understand before we tried to help?\\r\\n06\\r\\nIn September, I wrote about a choice we'd made with the CPG Playbook marketplace.\\n\\nWe could have made the directory look bigger by listing companies without their participation. We chose a smaller group that had agreed to be there.\\n\\nI'm still comfortable with that choice.\\n\\nRunning U-LUV has taught me how much a small brand depends on the people around the product. The co-packer. The broker. The distributor. The 3PL.\\n\\nA founder looking for a partner needs to know what a listing actually means.\\n\\nHas this business agreed to participate? What information do we have? What do I still need to ask before deciding whether we're a fit?\\n\\nThose are useful questions for us to answer clearly.\\n\\nA listing count only tells you how many entries are on a page. The definition behind that count matters.\\n\\nI want us to be clear about what we know as we build CPG Playbook, even when that makes the starting number smaller.\\n\\nGrowth matters to me. So does being able to explain what we've counted.\\r\\n173:CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.share_playbook(p_playbook_id uuid,p_shared boolean DEFAULT true)\\r\\n174-RETURNS uuid LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path=public,pg_temp AS $$\\r\\n175-DECLARE\\r\\n176- v_uid uuid := auth.uid();\\r\\n177- v_owner uuid;\\r\\n178- v_creator uuid;\\r\\n179- v_title text;\\r\\n180- v_thread uuid;\\r\\n181-BEGIN\\r\\n182- IF v_uid IS NULL THEN\\r\\n183- RAISE EXCEPTION 'Not authenticated' USING ERRCODE='42501';\\r\\n184- END IF;\\r\\n185- SELECT user_id,created_by_user_id,title,team_conversation_id\\r\\n186- INTO v_owner,v_creator,v_title,v_thread\\r\\n187- FROM playbooks WHERE id=p_playbook_id FOR UPDATE;\\r\\n188- IF NOT FOUND THEN\\r\\n189- RAISE EXCEPTION 'Playbook not found' USING ERRCODE='P0002';\\r\\n190- END IF;\\r\\n191- IF NOT public.can_manage_owner_scope(v_owner,v_uid)\\r\\n192- OR NOT COALESCE(v_creator=v_uid OR public.is_superadmin(v_uid),false) THEN\\r\\n193- RAISE EXCEPTION 'Only the playbook creator or workspace superadmin can share it' USING ERRCODE='42501';\\r\\n194- END IF;\\r\\n195- IF p_shared THEN\\r\\n196- IF v_thread IS NULL THEN\\r\\n197- INSERT INTO conversations(user_id,created_by_user_id,title)\\r\\n198- VALUES (v_owner,v_uid,left(v_title,200)) RETURNING id INTO v_thread;\\r\\n199- END IF;\\r\\n200- UPDATE playbooks SET visibility='workspace',team_conversation_id=v_thread,legacy_shared_conversation=false WHERE id=p_playbook_id;\\r\\n201- RETURN v_thread;\\r\\n202- END IF;\\r\\n203- UPDATE playbooks SET visibility='private' WHERE id=p_playbook_id;\\r\\n204- RETURN NULL;\\r\\n205-END $$;\\r\\n206:REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.share_playbook(uuid,boolean) FROM PUBLIC,anon;\\r\\n207:GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.share_playbook(uuid,boolean) TO authenticated,service_role;\\r\\n208:COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.share_playbook(uuid,boolean) IS\\r\\n209- 'The creator or current workspace superadmin shares a playbook with the workspace or takes it private again. Nothing is deleted either way.';\\r\\n210--- Keep shared editing, but only the recorded creator or an in-workspace\\r\\n211--- superadmin may archive, restore, reset, remove steps or delete a playbook.\\r\\n212--- Unknown historical creators stay null; workspace ownership is not authorship.\\r\\n213-CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.can_destroy_playbook(p_playbook_id uuid)\\r\\n214-RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER\\r\\n215-SET search_path=public,pg_temp AS $$\\r\\n216- SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM public.playbooks p\\r\\n217- WHERE p.id=p_playbook_id AND public.can_manage_owner_scope(p.user_id) AND public.can_access_playbook(p.id)\\r\\n218- AND (p.created_by_user_id=auth.uid() OR public.is_superadmin(auth.uid())))\\r\\n219-$$;\\r\\n220-REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.can_destroy_playbook(uuid) FROM PUBLIC,anon;\\r\\n221-GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.can_destroy_playbook(uuid) TO authenticated,service_role;\\r\\n222-\\r\\n223--- Keep removal and its untouched task in one transaction. Recheck authority\\r\\n224--- under the parent lock, so a refusal never leaves a partially cleared plan.\\r\\n225-CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.remove_playbook_step(p_step_id uuid)\\r\\n226-RETURNS jsonb LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path=public,pg_temp AS $$\\r\\n227-DECLARE v_book uuid; v_owner uuid; v_step public.playbook_steps; v_task public.tasks; v_kept boolean:=false;\\r\\n228-BEGIN\\r\\n229- IF auth.uid() IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Not authenticated' USING ERRCODE='42501'; END IF;\\r\\n230- SELECT playbook_id INTO v_book FROM playbook_steps WHERE id=p_step_id;\\r\\n231- IF NOT FOUND THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Step not found' USING ERRCODE='P0002'; END IF;\\r\\n232- SELECT user_id INTO v_owner FROM playbooks WHERE id=v_book FOR UPDATE;\\r\\n233- IF NOT public.can_destroy_playbook(v_book) THEN\\r\\n234- RAISE EXCEPTION 'Only the playbook creator or workspace superadmin can remove steps' USING ERRCODE='42501';\\r\\n235- END IF;\\r\\n236- SELECT * INTO v_step FROM playbook_steps WHERE id=p_step_id AND playbook_id=v_book FOR UPDATE;\\r\\n237- IF NOT FOUND THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Step not found' USING ERRCODE='P0002'; END IF;\\r\\n238- IF v_step.user_id IS DISTINCT FROM v_owner THEN\\r\\n239- RAISE EXCEPTION 'Step must belong to the same workspace' USING ERRCODE='23514';\\r\\n240- END IF;\\r\\n241- IF v_step.task_id IS NOT NULL THEN\\r\\n242- SELECT * INTO v_task FROM tasks WHERE id=v_step.task_id FOR UPDATE;\\r\\n243- IF FOUND THEN\\r\\n244- IF v_task.user_id IS DISTINCT FROM v_step.user_id OR v_task.playbook_id IS DISTINCT FROM v_book\\r\\n245- OR (v_task.step_id IS NOT NULL AND v_task.step_id IS DISTINCT FROM p_step_id) THEN\\r\\n246- RAISE EXCEPTION 'Task must belong to the same playbook' USING ERRCODE='23514';\\r\\n247- END IF;\\r\\n248- IF v_task.status IS NULL OR v_task.status='todo' THEN DELETE FROM tasks WHERE id=v_task.id;\\r\\n249- ELSE v_kept:=true; END IF;\\r\\n250- END IF;\\r\\n251- END IF;\\r\\n252- DELETE FROM playbook_steps WHERE id=p_step_id;\\r\\n253- UPDATE playbook_steps s SET step_number=ordered.number,sort_order=ordered.number-1\\r\\n254- FROM (SELECT id,row_number() OVER(ORDER BY sort_order,step_number,id)::integer AS number\\r\\n255- FROM playbook_steps WHERE playbook_id=v_book) ordered WHERE s.id=ordered.id;\\r\\n256- RETURN jsonb_build_object('title',v_step.title,'playbook_id',v_book,'step_id',p_step_id,'task_kept',v_kept);\\r\\n257-END $$;\\r\\n258-REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.remove_playbook_step(uuid) FROM PUBLIC,anon;\\r\\n259-GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.remove_playbook_step(uuid) TO authenticated,service_role;\\r\\n260-\\r\\n261--- A status-specific trigger preserves normal Team UPDATE access. However, **“Assigned to me” returns playbooks containing the viewer’s open steps**, not individual tasks (`book.ts:149`). It also matches confirmed typed names when no user ID exists (`book.ts:115`). That display fallback does not establish recipient identity for email.\n\n2. **FAIL — task-specific deep links.** Existing links such as “View related tasks” target `/tasks?playbook=…` (`src/components/layout/right-sidebar.tsx:117`), whose redirect loses the playbook. Assignment notices instead link to `/playbooks/` or `/guest/playbooks/`, without a step identifier (`supabase/migrations/20261007214042_guest_delivery_assignments.sql:266`). `/chat?playbook=` has an opening handler (`src/components/chat/chat-interface.tsx:3010`), but this does not provide an exact-task destination.\n\n3. **FAIL — consistent task assignment/reassignment.** The legacy task API supports self-assignment only; assigning or removing another user returns 403 (`src/app/api/tasks/[id]/assignees/route.ts:109`, `:177`). It writes `task_assignees` directly (`:142`), with no notification call. Migration references define self-assignment policies, without a task-assignment delivery trigger (`20260929021532_tenant_workspace_write_roles.sql:31`).\n\n Playbook steps use a separate assignment model. `manual_assign_step` resolves eligible people and writes through `assign_playbook_step_recipient` (`src/lib/playbooks/operations.ts:2575`). Its operation reports success even when a typed name resolves to no account; such a record cannot notify a recipient. This is a possible explanation to investigate, not Debbie/Jim’s established root cause.\n\n4. **PASS — durable step-assignment enqueueing; FAIL — notice context.** Confirmed assignment/reassignment to a different identified person creates a revision event, recipient notification and email outbox row transactionally (`20261007214042_guest_delivery_assignments.sql:216`). The newer book-bound command additionally checks expected revision and command identity Email non-delivery is not reproduced.**\\n\\n**PASS — release source.** HEAD is `9dda8392163e6e39eb8c893acd17aa3f01b3a967`; tree is `d969a1c143e2a4b1972e7ac0b64959590cb7dd18`. No tracked changes were reported. Remote main/prod equivalence remains parent-supplied evidence. Review was read-only.\\n\\n1. **FAIL — individual tasks across accessible playbooks.** `/tasks` redirects unconditionally to `/chat`, discarding query context (`src/app/(app)/tasks/page.tsx:11`). The retained `TasksView` queries tasks only for `effectiveOwnerId`, the active workspace (`src/hooks/use-tasks.ts:166`). Its filters cover playbook, module, priority and status, without assignee filtering (`src/components/tasks/tasks-view.tsx:191`; `src/components/tasks/use-task-filter-params.ts:66`).\\n\\n The current playbook book reads accessible playbooks without that owner restriction (`src/lib/playbooks/book.ts:301`). However, **“Assigned to me” returns playbooks containing the viewer’s open steps**, not individual tasks (`book.ts:149`). It also matches confirmed typed names when no user ID exists (`book.ts:115`). That display fallback does not establish recipient identity for email.\\n\\n2. **FAIL — task-specific deep links.** Existing links such as “View related tasks” target `/tasks?playbook=…` (`src/components/layout/right-sidebar.tsx:117`), whose redirect loses the playbook. Assignment notices instead link to `/playbooks/` or `/guest/playbooks/`, without a step identifier (`supabase/migrations/20261007214042_guest_delivery_assignments.sql:266`). `/chat?playbook=` has an opening handler (`src/components/chat/chat-interface.tsx:3010`), but this does not provide an exact-task destination.\\n\\n3. **FAIL — consistent task assignment/reassignment.** The legacy task API supports self-assignment only; assigning or removing another user returns 403 (`src/app/api/tasks/[id]/assignees/route.ts:109`, `:177`). It writes `task_assignees` directly (`:142`), with no notification call. Migration references define self-assignment policies, without a task-assignment delivery trigger (`20260929021532_tenant_workspace_write_roles.sql:31`).\\n\\n Playbook steps use a separate assignment model. `manual_assign_step` resolves eligible people and writes through `assign_playbook_step_recipient` (`src/lib/playbooks/operations.ts:2575`). Its operation reports success even when a typed name resolves to no account; such a record cannot notify a recipient. This is a possible explanation to investigate, not Debbie/Jim’s established root cause.\\n\\n4. **PASS — durable step-assignment enqueueing; FAIL — notice context.** Confirmed assignment/reassignment to a different identified person creates a revision event, recipient notification and email outbox row transactionally (`20261007214042_guest_delivery_assignments.sql:216`). The newer book-bound command additionally checks expected revision and command identity (`20261008011426_guest_manager_safe_preview_and_book_bound_assignment.sql:109`).\\n\\n The inbox title is only **“A task was assigned to you”**, omitting actor, task and playbook (`20261007214042_guest_delivery_assignments.sql:455`). Email includes task title, playbook title and description, but omits the assigning actor (`src/lib/notify/delivery-render.ts:46`). The assignment delivery DTO also lacks actor display information (`src/lib/notify/delivery-contracts.ts:54`).\\n\\n5. **PASS — delivery safeguards in source; NOT RUN — delivery reliability in production.** The pad calls the assignment-status endpoint after a successful identified assignment (`src/components/chat/unit-pad.tsx:1339`); queued/paused status wakes the worker (`src/lib/notify/step-assigned.ts:8`). The worker persists transport outcomes and does not automatically resend an uncertain request (`src/lib/notify/delivery-worker.ts:50`). Resolution suppresses obsolete assignment revisions or lost eligibility (`20261007214042_guest_delivery_assignments.sql:253`).\\n\\n A periodic recovery runner exists, but requires deployment configuration (`scripts/delivery-runner.mjs:7`). Its deployed schedule, sender configuration, queue health and Jim’s delivery receipts were not inspected.\\n\\n**Smallest complete repairs and acceptance checks:**\\n\\n- Add an individual-task view to the current workroom, using existing access rules and simple assignee/status/playbook filters. Define explicitly whether it covers all accessible playbooks; preserve private-thread and Guest boundaries. Do not merely remove the workspace predicate: current task authorization also requires owner scope and source privacy (`20261020031500_preserve_thread_task_privacy.sql:90`).\\n- Use confirmed account IDs for actionable assignments. Keep typed suggestions distinct. Decide how legacy `task_assignees` relates to step ownership before implementing task filtering.\\n- Include permitted actor name, task and playbook in notices; add an exact-step destination. Update inbox destination validation alongside links (`src/lib/notify/inbox.ts:7`). Preserve current email preferences and delivery safeguards.\\n- Verify assignment, duplicate submission, reassignment, revoked access, ambiguous delivery and filtered task navigation. Reassignment must invalidate obsolete recipient notices/deliveries.\\n\\nFocused regression targets: `book.test.ts`, `assigned.test.ts`, `playbooks-book.test.tsx`, `unit-pad.test.tsx`, `delivery-render.test.ts`, `delivery-worker.test.ts`, `use-tasks.test.tsx`, and the task-assignees route tests. Run selected files with `pnpm exec vitest run `; assignment authorization requires the existing isolated DB suites.\\n\\n**NOT RUN:** tests, browser walkthroughs, database checks, deployed worker configuration, provider acceptance and mailbox receipt. Before allowing fixture writes, inspect schedulers and keep workers, outreach, publishing and paid-provider activity disabled. Existing comment-generation tests require separate provider authorization; this harness does not grant it. Begin hosted validation with `e2e/role-fixtures.spec.ts` when that environment is authorized.\\r\\n\\r\\nSet these through local environment variables or a protected CI environment, never in tracked files or chat:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Variable | Required value |\\r\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\\r\\n| `SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` | The same isolated `https://.supabase.co` origin |\\r\\n| `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`, `VITE_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID`, `E2E_ISOLATED_PROJECT_REF` | The same isolated project reference; the last value explicitly acknowledges fixture writes |\\r\\n| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Isolated backend key, used only by setup/cleanup |\\r\\n| `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Isolated public key, used for separate actor logins and caller-scoped reads |\\r\\n| `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL` | Matching app origin; defaults to `http://localhost:8080` |\\r\\n\\r\\nThe shared ClawLI backend is rejected. The harness starts a local dev server when needed; an existing preview must run this candidate against the same isolated backend. Source environment variables alone do not prove that a remote preview matches. Keep the service key out of frontend variables. No existing test logins are needed: setup creates disposable identities with random passwords, without sending invitations.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Explicit actors and organizations\\r\\n\\r\\nEach run creates two uniquely named organizations, A and B. Each actor has a distinct auth user, login client, storage-state file and, through the `actors` fixture, browser context. The ordinary `page` uses the member session and must load the authenticated dashboard before assertions run. Auth redirects cannot satisfy negative permission checks.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Actor | Organization memberships | Application role |\\r\\n| ------------ | ------------------------ | ---------------- |\\r\\n| `owner` | A: owner | user |\\r\\n| `admin` | A: manager | admin |\\r\\n| `member` | A: member, B: member | user |\\r\\n| `outsider` | B: member; none in A | user |\\r\\n| `superadmin` | B: member; none in A | super_admin |\\r\\n\\r\\n`manager` is the schema's workspace administration role. It is distinct from the application `admin` role. The super-admin fixture can exercise the existing switched-organization semantics without silently adding membership in A. Membership in two organizations enables caller-scoped isolation checks; it does not imply the UI exposes ordinary-member organization switching.\\r\\n\\r\\nSignup-trigger personal workspaces are recorded and removed by exact ID before login, so they cannot become the selected workspace. A synthetic active subscription and one member-owned deal are seeded. Legacy helpers create any additional identities only inside A/B; hard-coded shared organization names are gone. Tenant fixtures require an explicit run-owned organization. The hosted role smoke independently checks token identity, every expected membership and application role, and loads each dashboard. Full permission and private-memory acceptance is still deferred.\\r\\n\\r\\nRLS denial tests first require an authorized read of the exact seeded row, including invite and synthetic audit fixtures. A backend that denies every read cannot satisfy the test. Masking checks require the uniquely named seeded card and its expected mask state; unrelated cards cannot satisfy them. Invite tests use separate member/admin sessions and require the expected Team/form controls. An invalid-token test requires the precise API rejection as well as the UI error; a network or server outage cannot count as successful validation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Exact cleanup and recovery\\r\\n\\r\\nThe ignored directory `e2e/.auth//` holds separate role sessions and an append-only `ledger.jsonl`. The ledger records intended IDs **before** requests, then deletion receipts after independent absence checks. It excludes passwords, tokens and content. Session files contain credentials: never commit or upload them as CI artifacts.\\r\\n\\r\\nCleanup discovers browser-created IDs only in the two run-owned organizations, using stable ID pagination. Its explicit table inventory covers the root suites' accounts, leads, deals, posts, queue, activities and Engine execution receipts. It journals each discovered ID and deletes children before parents. Database cascades handle dependent records such as generated comments and auth-owned profiles/default roles; actual hosted cascade behavior remains an isolated-environment gate. A new suite that writes other tables or storage objects must extend the cleanup inventory and regression checks before being enabled.\\r\\n\\r\\nThere are no user-wide or organization-wide delete statements. Every delete names a recorded row ID. Untracked explicit IDs, wrong-project recovery, failed reads, API errors and rows still present after deletion fail cleanup. A failed child prevents parent deletion. Setup failure invokes cleanup once; cleanup failure retains the ledger and sessions and fails the run. Per-test deletion failures mark the run `cleanup-failed` immediately. Fixture creation, membership/status updates and per-test deletions reject both `cleanup-failed` and `cleaned` runs. This includes parent-user cleanup in a test's `finally` block, which must not cascade away evidence after a child failed. Only ordered `cleanupFixtures` recovery remains allowed. A truncated ledger also fails closed. One worker and sequential tests are enforced to prevent concurrent journal writers.\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter diagnosing a failure, recover the **same** run explicitly, with the same environment. never reset `gl.info` anywhere else, or the published draw counts lose passes.\\r\\nSurface maps are KTX2 sets built by `scripts/assets/textures.py` (1k ETC1S for every tier, `hq/` 2k colour and UASTC normals on balanced and high) and loaded only through `pbr()`/`ktx2Texture()`, which hand out placeholder textures filled in place and held behind `PbrGate`; never load a JPG/PNG surface map beside them.\\r\\nEvery kit slot is photographic: painted trim, metal and poles use the neutral `paint`/`metal`/`pole` sets with a colour gain equal to the reciprocal of the set's mean albedo, so vertex paint keeps its brightness.\\r\\nKit glass is interior-mapped (`interiorWindows.ts`): panes keep their box UVs and carry an `interior` (room, seed) attribute written by `Kit.add` from its `room` option (`data/rooms.ts`), so the house generator sets real rooms by passing `room` and nothing else changes; lit panes are the `glassLit` slot.\\r\\nShadow-casting directional lights are the sun and its cascades, mounted by `Daylight` finest first; the patched `lights_fragment_begin` (`cascades.ts`) takes the sun's shadow from the finest cascade holding a fragment, so add no other shadow-casting directional light.\\r\\nOutdoor materials take the weather patch (`weatherPatch.ts`) wherever they take lamp pools (kit, outdoor static buckets); cloud shadows dim only the sun, through the `SUN_CLOUD_SHADOW` hook, so indoor materials must never take it.\\r\\nLook patches that must survive the static batch's material clones (car flake, street probe) mark `userData` and are re-applied by `reapplyLook`.\\r\\nThe street reflection probe (`ReflectionProbe.tsx`) refreshes only on a new quarter-hour, weather kind or 40 m cell, one cube face per frame; never update it per frame, and keep the sky's sun disc hidden while it captures (the disc overflows half float and one infinite texel turns every reflection black), and capture only once every shadow-casting light has a rendered map (a face drawn before the shadow pass, including the first after a restored context, binds an empty texture to the shadow samplers, an invalid draw). A lost context withdraws the published capture (users fall back to the sky environment) until the recapture publishes, and the lost-context GPU release (`isLostContextRelease`) never drops probe registrations; only a real dispose does.\\r\\nThe modded grade is a 32³ LUT baked in code (`gradeLut.ts`) applied after tone mapping inside the merged effect pass, and eye adaptation (`exposure.ts`, high tier) corrects only part of the way toward its key, so tuned daylight holds; A/B the tone mapper through `core/look`, never by editing PostFX.\\r\\nAgent desk monitors are one canvas per workstation (the `agent` kind in `codeScreens.ts`) redrawn only when that agent's log or state changes, at most two per tick; agents draw with distance LOD (draw range per tier, head kit and sun shadow only up close) and their nameplates are laid out once per frame, capped and decluttered by priority.\\r\\nStreet cars (traffic and the kerbside parked) are drawn by `fleet/Traffic.tsx` as one BatchedMesh per car finish with per-instance paint, built from the fleet's real-scale models unscaled (`data/carModels`, glazed like the drive cars per tier), so their draws stay fixed however many cars or colours, and beyond `FAR_FROM` (per tier: sooner on the lower tiers, never hidden) a car switches its instances to the generator's simplified `-far.glb` (coarse tyres, no cabin); never give a street car its own meshes.\\r\\nGenerated interiors (`kit/interiors.ts`, one merged mesh per interior slot) are built a few milliseconds per frame within 30 m into an LRU and drawn only while you are inside or the front door stands open near you; their light is baked per vertex (the room's lamp, contact shading) and added by the indoor patch (`indoorLight.ts`), never by real lights, and interior slots never take lamp pools or the weather.\\r\\nThe time-of-day look is one keyed table (`core/timecycle`, thirteen GTA-style keys): sun, sky fill, bounce, fog, exposure, bloom, saturation, vignette and grain are tuned there and read from `tod`, never as per-view curves; weather offsets come from `core/weather` presets.\\r\\nFog is the height-fog patch (`heightFog.ts`) of the shared fog chunks, its extra uniforms carried by reference on the shader library; a custom shader that includes the fog chunks without them falls back to plain linear fog, and a multiply decal replaces the fog colour through `fogFragmentWith`, never by editing the chunk text.\\r\\nThe default tone mapper is the GTA Hable curve (`gtaTone.ts`, its own exposure uniform); contrast lives in that curve, so add no contrast effect and keep the LUT gentle.\\r\\nNight lights beyond the real lamps are one instanced draw (`DistantLights.tsx`) built from the road graph at load; coronas (`GlowSprites.tsx`) fade by a round-robin collision-index test, never a depth readback.\\r\\nStreet props are one BatchedMesh on one atlas material (`StreetProps.tsx`) placed only from `data/streetProps`, whose footprints `systems/streetProps` registers, so a new prop kind goes into the atlas script, the placement data and nothing else. Props beyond `PROP_DRAW` (per tier) of the camera are hidden; ez-tree street trees draw their full model within `TREE_LOD_NEAR` on Balanced and the reduced `-lod1` model beyond (High full everywhere, Low reduced everywhere), so every tree stays drawn.\\r\\nStreet cars swap detail through the dithered crossfade (`lodFade.ts`): each batch draws its own clone of a finish (re-patched with `reapplyLook`, glow copied from the shared finish each frame), so never hand a street-car batch the shared finish itself.\\r\\n`StudioLife.tsx` keeps the studio's moving parts at a small fixed draw cost: static parts merge into one mesh per finish, indicator lights and blind fabric are instanced, each live surface (ship board, TV, lobby screen, tablet, ON AIR) is one canvas texture redrawn only when its signature changes and at most once a second, and the whole set hides away from the house.\\r\\n\\r\\nEdge smoothing is SMAA in its own last effect group on display-referred colour (hardware MSAA only where AO is off), and the adaptive quality ladder in `core/quality.ts` is pure functions (it sheds supersampling, then AO, then MSAA, before any resolution), so the performance monitor and tests share one source of truth.\\r\\nThe low tier buys draw calls with nuance, never with content: the static batch merges untextured surfaces in coarser roughness/metalness steps and the neighbourhood kit builds as one chunk (no culling), because phones are draw-bound long before triangle-bound.\\r\\nGraphics tiers cut triangles without changing what stands in the world: the low tier thins tree crowns to fewer, larger leaf cards and every tree tube is open-ended (caps are always buried or inside the crown), so the scene reads the same on every device.\\r\\nStreet fixtures, trees and footprints share data/layout; photographic props use data/streetProps. StreetProps batches attach and dispose within one effect, preventing replay from drawing freed textures.\\r\\nDraw calls and triangles are read once per frame after post-processing (`views/FrameStats`, renderer counters with `autoReset` off) and published as `window.__mansionPerf` in dev builds or with `?perf`; `scripts/bench/frames.py baseline` logs them per fixed view and tier, and `docs/perf-baseline.md` holds the numbers to stay within.\\r\\nPlayer gait timing uses pure `views/people/locomotion` rules so crossfades stay in phase at actual ground speed.\\r\\nPeopleGate requests atlases before its GLB hook suspends so downloads overlap without untextured people.\\r\\nPeople bodies load through `people/bodyLoad` (`loadBody`, `useBodies`, `usePeopleAssets`), which swaps in a street body when a body's file still fails after the asset retries; build the person and read measures with the returned id, because one missing body file must never blank the world.\\r\\nThe canvas holds frames until shader warmup finishes, so even a demand invalidation cannot render before warmup. Warmup borrows the composer's target, and the sky probe and ceiling-light visibility are initialized before it, so the first playable frame uses the warmed shader variants.\\r\\nThe world steps in `Loop` at useFrame priority -100 (after FrameStats at -1000) and the player root places itself at -50, so every view and the camera draw the same step; procedural poses refresh parent matrices with `updateWorldMatrix(true, true)` because a moved root's parent matrix is otherwise last frame's.\\r\\nLoad several GLTFs with `useGltfs` (`views/useGltfs`), never `useGLTF([...])`: drei caches a list under one key, so a file also loaded alone downloads and parses twice; models requested only by late Scene children are preloaded at the top of `Scene` because React stops rendering siblings once one suspends.\\r\\nThe library's locomotion cycles are reshaped once at fit time (`people/gaitShape.ts` via `rig.ts`: swing scaled about the cycle's mean, pelvis eased upright with the thighs compensated, running arms brought in, re-timed to human cadence); judge changes on `/debug-gait` (side and front filmstrips plus `window.__gait` metrics), never from gameplay shots.\\r\\n`?soak&film` holds the frame loop once the world is ready and `views/FilmClock` advances it one exact step at a time (`scripts/soak/film.py` saves frames and joins them into 30 fps clips), so motion is judged at full game speed on a slow software renderer.\\r\\nFilm-only follow cameras are placed after the world camera and before character poses; crew and pedestrian handles are exposed in film mode so captures can follow real walkers rather than replaying player input.\\r\\nStanding still, the player and crew run `applyStandStraight` after the mixer (pelvis lifted out of the idle's knee sag by `standLift`, trunk eased upright, feet under the hips by two-bone reach keeping the clip's foot height, shoulders squared, arms closer), and the drive pose reclines the back to a measured target (`DRIVE_RECLINE`) then `fitUnderRoof`, because the library's idle and sit clips stand crooked and hunch; `data/seatFit.test.ts` keeps every character inside every car.\\r\\nBald characters (`head.hair === \\\"none\\\"`) pass `bald` to `makePerson`, which cuts the hair part in the people material and its shadow depth material (`personDepthMaterial`); tinting alone cannot hide hair geometry, and a missing depth cut leaves a hair-shaped shadow.\\r\\nPlanted feet (`applyFootPlant` in `sitPose.ts`) run after the trunk pose for the player and crew within `PLANT_NEAR` of the camera, never for street pedestrians; ankle height is learnt per rig in world metres above the root. The lens effect drops its motion history on a camera cut (`CUT_MOVE`/`CUT_TURN`) and on a `gpuEpoch()` bump.\\r\\nEvery asset download retries server and network failures a few times (`core/assetRetry`, installed on three's FileLoader), and the street trees sit behind their own boundary that falls back to procedural trees, because a brief hosting error must never blank the world.\\r\\nAuthored car glass never keeps refraction (`KHR_materials_transmission`): `authoredCarRig` turns it into tinted blending with depth writes off, because one visible transmissive surface makes three re-render the whole opaque world each frame and opaque glass without depth writes flickers as the draw order changes.\\r\\nA fleet car or bike changes its detail level inside a React transition (`fleetLod` picks it, the first pick from the real distance) and preloads its other levels, so a level change keeps the drawn model on screen instead of flashing the box stand-in while the next file downloads.\\r\\n209: * The edge of the map: the only walk and drive bound left. piping\\\":{\\\"color\\\":[0.23000000417232513,0.25999999046325684,0.20000000298023224],\\\"roughness\\\":0.8799999952316284,\\\"metalness\\\":0,\\\"provider\\\":null,\\\"normalStrength\\\":0,\\\"opacity\\\":1,\\\"emissive\\\":[1,1,1],\\\"emissiveIntensity\\\":0},\\\"missing|lounge-rug\\\":{\\\"color\\\":[0.38,0.323,0.227],\\\"roughness\\\":1,\\\"metalness\\\":0,\\\"provider\\\":\\\"fabric\\\",\\\"normalStrength\\\":0,\\\"opacity\\\":1,\\\"emissive\\\":[0,0,0],\\\"emissiveIntensity\\\":0}}\\r\\nA gamepad is polled in `input.ts` and writes the same input fields the keys do (triggers are the pedals in a car and climb / throttle in the air, by the mode the fleet sets each step with `setPadMode`); the keys take over again as soon as the pad goes quiet.\\r\\nThe studio publishes everything audible as a `StudioEvent` with its world position (`onStudioEvent` in `studio.ts`: radio station, espresso, ON AIR, blinds, light scenes, TV, the front desk's greeting); the audio system subscribes (`studioAudio.ts`: the lounge soundbar is a room receiver on the radio through `setRoomRadio`, tuned to the car dial's stations in `data/radio`) and plays them on its own buses, and the studio never drives the mixer.\\r\\nStudio interactions by agents come only from the station model: an agent the assigner put on the coffee spot pulls a shot on arrival, one on a ship-board spot is \\\"at the board\\\"; nothing in `studio.ts` moves or steers an agent.\\r\\n`agents.send` always settles (`settleSend` in `agents/link`: a rejection or a link silent for 15 s becomes `{ ok: false, error }`), so no TideOS app waits forever on an intent.\\r\\nPedestrians (`pedestrians.ts`) walk only the street layer of the city nav graph (`streetNav`, read from the road graph at runtime), keep right so oncoming walkers pass, wait at the kerb for `crossingClear` before a crosswalk and publish whoever is on one for the traffic to brake for (`fleet/walkers.ts`); their pure rules (graph, density by hour, turns, crossing gaps, diving clear of a car, fleeing, the nearest sidewalk) live in `pedestrianRules.ts` with the tests. They also take over drivers pulled out of stolen cars and react to frights and the fleet's fast cars (`dangerCars`): off the graph a pedestrian is `loose` (pulled, stumble, shout, dive, then straight for the nearest sidewalk), collides like any walker, and is published as a crosser so the traffic brakes for them.\\r\\nClimbing over fences and low walls (`vault.ts`) is pure: a collider flagged `climb` (thin lot fences up to 1.9 m) or any thin box up to 1.3 m is climbable when the player pushes square into it and presses Jump, with free floor at about the same height beyond; vehicles and standable boxes never are. The same file's `fellThrough` is the ground safety net: feet far under the floor go back to the last spot they stood on. Space held from a jump started early still catches the fence in the air, a climb landing with Space held never springs into a jump, and the HUD shows `CLIMB_HINT` while `canClimb()`; re-run `scripts/ground/sweep.ts` (fences, ground, curbs over the whole map, under bun with the cache variable) after changing walking, floors, walls or fences (it also sprints into every thin wall at a normal frame and a 0.1 s hitch). The player move is sub-stepped to 0.15 m between collision passes, so no speed or frame hitch tunnels a wall.\\r\\nGait speeds (gait.ts) are chosen so each locomotion cycle plays within about 15% of its reshaped ground speed (`clipSpeed` in `views/people/locomotion`); retune speeds, not playback caps, or strides look floaty or frantic.\\r\\nStart, stop, skid and pivot moves and the lean into curves (`footMoves.ts`) are pure rules read from ground speed and turn rate only; the views turn them into a trunk pose after the mixer (`views/people/footMovesPose.ts`), so there are no extra clips and the legs keep the planted gait.\\r\\nFoot contact (`footContact.ts`) is pure: a foot near the ground and slow plants and locks its world point, releasing on lift or when out of reach; the views solve legs toward it after the mixer. The player keeps only `PUSH_SLACK` over its collision-resolved travel, so a blocked body stands instead of cycling its legs.\\r\\n\",\"exit_code\":0,\"status\":\"completed\"}} | {\"type\":\"item.completed\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_28\",\"type\":\"agent_message\",\"text\":\"**PASS — read-only diagnosis.
